title: NEB Class 11 Biology — Introductory Microbiology — 2024
subject: biology
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: What are the characteristic features of bacteria? Give one example each of beneficial and harmful bacteria.
questions.solution:
**Bacteria (Monera):** prokaryotic, unicellular, no true nucleus, peptidoglycan wall, binary fission.

Beneficial: *Rhizobium* (nitrogen fixation), *Lactobacillus* (curd). Harmful: *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* (TB), *Salmonella typhi* (typhoid).
questions.knowledgeNote: Shapes: cocci (spheres), bacilli (rods), spirilla (spirals) — shape vocabulary recurs in one-markers.

questions.question: Why are viruses considered to be on the borderline between living and non-living? Give reasons.
questions.solution:
**Living traits:** carry genetic material (DNA/RNA), mutate and evolve, multiply inside hosts.

**Non-living traits:** no cell, no metabolism, no response to stimuli; crystallisable like chemicals (Stanley, TMV).

Hence the borderline — alive only inside a host cell.
questions.knowledgeNote: Viruses are obligate parasites: zero independent metabolism, which is why antibiotics cannot touch them.

questions.question: Describe the lytic cycle of a bacteriophage with a diagram description.
questions.solution: (1) **Attachment:** tail fibres grip the bacterial wall. (2) **Penetration:** DNA injected, capsid outside. (3) **Biosynthesis:** host machinery hijacked to make viral DNA and proteins. (4) **Maturation:** new phages assembled. (5) **Lysis:** lysozyme bursts the cell, ~100–200 virions released.
questions.knowledgeNote: Lytic (kill now) vs lysogenic (prophage sleeps) — the two viral lifestyles behind one more comparison question.

questions.question: What is Gram staining? Distinguish between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
questions.solution:
**Gram staining** (Christian Gram) separates bacteria by wall structure: crystal violet → iodine → alcohol wash → safranin counterstain.

**Gram-positive:** thick peptidoglycan retains violet (e.g. *Staphylococcus*). **Gram-negative:** thin wall, outer membrane — violet washes out, stains pink (e.g. *E. coli*).
questions.knowledgeNote: The stain predicts antibiotics: penicillin hits Gram-positive walls; Gram-negative outer membranes resist it.

questions.question: What are cyanobacteria? Explain their role in nitrogen fixation with an example.
questions.solution:
**Cyanobacteria** (blue-green algae) are photosynthetic prokaryotes — the first oxygen producers.

Heterocyst-forming types (*Nostoc, Anabaena*) fix atmospheric N₂ via nitrogenase in low-oxygen heterocysts, enriching paddy fields — the original biofertiliser of Asian rice farming.
questions.knowledgeNote: Azolla–Anabaena symbiosis in paddies fixes ~30–60 kg N/ha free — traditional farming's nitrogen factory.

questions.question: Write any four economic importances of microbes.
questions.solution: (1) Dairy: *Lactobacillus* curd/cheese. (2) Medicine: *Penicillium* antibiotics, yeast insulin. (3) Biogas/bioremediation: methanogens digest waste. (4) Agriculture: *Rhizobium* biofertiliser; (5) industry: yeast brewing, *Aspergillus* citric acid.
questions.knowledgeNote: One beneficial + one harmful example per group is the safest answering pattern for 'importance' questions.
